URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory_safety
Summary: Memory safety is the state of being protected from various software bugs and security vulnerabilities when dealing with memory access, such as buffer overflows and dangling pointers. By contrast, programming languages like C, C++, and Fortran allow arbitrary pointer arithmetic with pointers implemented as direct memory addresses with no provision for bounds checking, making them memory-unsafe.

Rust is a general-purpose language that emphasizes performance, type safety, concurrency, and memory safety [1]. It supports multiple paradigms and was influenced by functional programming ideas such as immutability, higher-order functions, and pattern matching [1].

Rust is a general-purpose language that balances performance, type safety, concurrency, and memory safety [1]. Its multi-paradigm design draws on functional programming ideas [1].

For example, Java is memory-safe because its runtime error detection checks array bounds and pointer dereferences. By contrast, programming languages like C, C++, and Fortran allow arbitrary pointer arithmetic with pointers implemented as direct memory addresses with no provision for bounds checking, making them memory-unsafe.
